messages:
nina: quick heads-up — during ProtoX14B int4 canary we saw a P99 latency jump after the eviction tweak landed. not huge QPS loss but tail is bad.

devon: ugh. can you paste the run summary?

nina: sure. benchbot run attached below (canary group A = old evict, B = new evict).

benchbot: ```
run_id: protox-int4-evict-2026-03-20T18:04Z
qps: 25
model: ProtoX14B-int4
group A (old): p50=45ms p95=120ms p99=210ms error_rate=0.3%
group B (new): p50=47ms p95=150ms p99=420ms error_rate=0.7%
memory: mean_rss_mb A=16240 B=16180
OOMs: 0
notes: increased p99 coincident with eviction threshold change + aggressive slot compaction
```

alex: interesting that mean RSS is slightly lower but tail doubled. smells like fragmentation/latency during KV compaction + kernel preemption. did we see CPU spikes on the host?

nina: host cpu shows 10-15% sys spikes during some tails, but mostly GPU kernel stalls reported in the runtime trace. attaching small snippet.

nina: ```
[trace] 18:04:12.102 kernel_enqueue cudaStreamSynchronize -> wait 24ms
[trace] 18:04:12.126 kv_compact: start 18:04:12.126 -> finish 18:04:12.198 (72ms)
[trace] 18:04:12.220 kernel_enqueue -> wait 110ms
```

maria_g: could be eviction-induced scatter causing additional page faults or host<->device memcpy thrash. new evict was lowering per-slot keep_time from 10s -> 2s right?

devon: yes we shortened shelf-life to free up slots faster for small convo workloads. rationale was to reduce mem pressure for high-concurrency. forgot to gate it by model size.

alex: hypothesize: aggressive eviction increases churn on KV cache for long-context tokens on ProtoX14B which produces cache misses and forces larger KV reconstructions, causing GPU stalls and host mem copies -> p99 spikes.

maria_g: we should try two quick repros: 1) restore keep_time to 10s for ProtoX only, 2) keep new keep_time but reduce max_batch_size from 8->4 to reduce microburst KV churn.

nina: I ran (2) quickly: max_batch=4 produced p99=230ms (much better than 420) but qps dropped ~12%.

devon: thanks — that suggests batching is amplifying the eviction effect. can you paste the perf config?

nina: ```
config A (old): keep_time=10s max_batch=8 prefetch=false eviction_policy=LRU
config B (new): keep_time=2s max_batch=8 prefetch=false eviction_policy=LRU+compact
config C (mitigate): keep_time=2s max_batch=4 prefetch=false eviction_policy=LRU+compact
```

alex: another quick test to try: enable prefix prefetch (warm KV ahead) for ProtoX. if eviction is unavoidable, prefetch mitigates misses at cost of some CPU/GPU memory but might flatten tails.

maria_g: agree. also we should test a hybrid: keep_time=3s + max_batch=6 + prefetch=true. find the sweet spot for throughput vs tail.

devon: can someone run C and the hybrid overnight and post p95/p99/delta to master ticket? I'll tag infra to hold off on global rollout of the new evict policy until we have model-specific guards.

nina: scheduled runs now (will take ~6h to get stable p99). starting with C then hybrid.

benchbot: queued: protox-int4-mitigate-C, protox-int4-mitigate-hybrid. estimated completion 6-8h.

alex: FYI we should also check fragmentation metrics on the allocator (free_slots vs contiguous_free). if compacting frequently increases fragmentation it can paradoxically increase host<->device transfers.

maria_g: good call — adding allocator debug counters to the runs.

devon: if both mitigations help, plan: revert global shelf-life change, create model override map: ProtoX14B -> keep_time=3s, default keep_time=2s. sync with rollout team.

nina: marking this thread owner: nina for data dump + devon for rollout plan. will update with benchbot results when done. :white_check_mark:
